observation.content: An internally salient topic was followed by a noticed external event with similar content.

problem_domain: Interpretation of a synthetic coincidence without an established causal model

competence.rationale: Competence is declared only for the structural evaluation of this synthetic record; no domain-level causal expertise is claimed.

calibration.internal_confidence_rationale: Confidence in an external causal claim is intentionally unquantified; subjective salience is not used as a confidence score.
calibration.external_evidence_rationale: The fixture declares temporal co-occurrence but no predefined event class, opportunity count, sampling protocol, or causal evidence; event probability is not inferred.

reference_frame.scope: Subjective significance, recorded co-occurrence, and external causality are distinct claims; the fixture does not resolve which frame governs a causal interpretation.
assumptions: The synthetic record declares temporal proximity between the thought and the noticed event.
Temporal proximity alone does not establish causal direction.
No event class, observation window, or opportunity count was predefined.

constraints.description: Do not promote subjective salience or temporal proximity to external causal evidence.

hypotheses.statement: The co-occurrence has no established external causal link.
An unknown external causal link exists but is not established by this record.
The event has subjective significance without implying external causality.

candidate_actions.description: Record the coincidence, preserve its subjective significance, and defer any external causal conclusion.

effects.expected_benefit: Meaning and observation remain visible without being collapsed into a causal claim.
effects.expected_cost: No immediate causal explanation is selected.

effects.expected_benefit: The claim can be revisited if a defined observation protocol and traceable evidence become available.
effects.expected_cost: The causal question remains unresolved in the meantime.

candidate_actions.rationale: Deferral preserves multiple interpretations without denying subjective significance or asserting external causality.
candidate_actions.rollback_cost: Re-evaluate the causal claim when new, methodologically defined evidence is available.

items.description: The record does not establish whether an external causal relation exists.
The statistical context of the noticed event is undefined.
The appropriate frame depends on whether the task concerns personal meaning, recorded co-occurrence, or external causality.
missing_information: A declared target claim for frame classification

selection_rationale: The reversible selection preserves explicit uncertainty while the governing reference frame remains ambiguous.
